title: Không
summary: Different ways to say Không in Vietnam start with a clear no, then add warmth when needed.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Không is the simple no. It is useful because many traveler moments need a clear answer before politeness or explanation. If you are declining an offer, Không, cảm ơn is warmer. If you are answering a direct yes/no question, Không can be enough.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use Không when the answer is no and the other person needs clarity more than extra explanation.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: The word is also the no/not piece inside many longer phrases.

sections.title: Softer no
sections.body: When the no is a refusal, add the phrase that keeps the moment friendly.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it to answer a direct question, correct a mistaken assumption, say an item is not yours, or decline when the other person is waiting for a clear yes/no answer.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: A bare Không can sound abrupt if you are turning down a person. Add cảm ơn when the person offered you something or helped you.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: These help you keep the no friendly or reassuring.

phrases.vietnamese: Không, cảm ơn, có thể để sau
phrases.pronunciation: khong cam on co the de sau
